summary: Extends the RTP payload format for uncompressed studio-quality video from RFC 4175 to support additional color sampling modes. It is standards-track.

eli5.summary: Studio video has many ways of storing color. This adds more of those ways to the method for sending raw video over the internet.

questions: what is rtp uncompressed video colour sampling
how to signal 16 bit rgb video in sdp
subtitle: Six extra colour sampling modes for raw video over RTP, such as 5-6-5 bit RGB.

tldr.problem: The uncompressed video payload format in RFC 4175 assumes the same number of bits for each colour component, so video such as 5-6-5 RGB cannot be signalled.
tldr.mechanism: This memo defines six new sampling modes (RGB+, RG+B, R+GB, BGR+, BG+R, B+GR) where the component marked with + gets one more bit than the value of the depth parameter.
tldr.outcome: Such formats, most commonly depth=5, can now be described in SDP and pack a pixel into two octets without padding.

today: RFC 4421 is a Proposed Standard and updates RFC 4175. No later RFC obsoletes it.

sections.title: The Signalling Gap
sections.content:
RFC 4175 packetises uncompressed, studio-quality video for RTP and lets sender and receiver agree on image size, colour space, pixel depth and colour sampling mode. Its signalling assumes the same number of bits for every colour component.

So 8 bits each for red, green and blue (24 bits per pixel) can be signalled, but 5 bits for red and blue with 6 for green (16 bits per pixel) cannot, even though the payload format can carry it.
sections.eli5: The old rules could only say 'every colour gets the same amount of detail'. This document lets one colour get a bit more.

sections.title: The Six New Sampling Modes
sections.content:
The new modes are RGB+, RG+B, R+GB, BGR+, BG+R and B+GR. They use the same sample packing order as the RGB and BGR modes, except that the component marked + MUST use one extra bit of colour depth.

The mandatory parameter depth=N gives N bits for the unmarked components and N+1 for the marked one. The main use is depth=5, which lets a pixel fit into two octets without padding. Other depths MAY be used.
sections.eli5: The plus sign marks which colour gets one extra bit of detail.

sections.title: An SDP Example
sections.content:
The memo shows 5-6-5 RGB video, 16 bits per pixel, signalled in SDP with sampling=RG+B, depth=5, width=1024 and height=768, in a media description using payload type 99 and raw/90000.

The IANA section extends the video/raw media type with the six values for its sampling parameter. The security considerations of RFC 4175 apply, and no new ones are added.
sections.eli5: The example tells the receiver: green is the one with the extra bit, and each colour gets five bits otherwise.
